messages:
maya: Hey all — landing my first PR to infra/runtime. Quick q: what's the preferred commit strategy here? squash? multiple commits? also what branch should I target for a small bugfix vs a feature?

alex: Welcome! For small bugfixes we prefer a single logical commit. For features, keep commits focused but squash before merge if they include noise. We use Conventional Commits in the changelog.

priya: We put the target branch as main for day-to-day work. If it's a backport include a PR to release/<semver>.

matt: Also check CODEOWNERS — if it touches eng-runtime it auto-requests reviewers. If CI is flaky ping me or add 'rerun ci' label.

ci-bot: redwood-ci: checks queued — lint, unit-tests, typecheck, integration-smoke. See https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/12345

maya: thanks — any tips for commit message format? can you paste a short example?

alex: Yep. We use Conventional Commits + short body. Example:

```
fix(runtime): fix kv cache invalidation on early exit
\nThe kv cache wasn't cleared when a request aborted early which caused stale prefix hits.
\nCo-authored-by: Maya <maya@redwood.ai>
```
\nKeep subject < 72 chars.

priya: Also add a one-line 'why' in the body and reference issue/PR if relevant. Use `Resolves #123` if it closes something.

matt: Pre-commit hooks run automatically on CI but run locally with:

```
pre-commit run --all-files
poetry run pytest -q
```
\nIf you get a lint error run `ruff format` / `ruff check`.

maya: got it. what's the convention for branch names?

alex: branch names: `user/<name>/short-desc` for features, `bug/<short-issue>` for fixes, or `hotfix/<ticket>` for urgent release fixes. Example: `bug/maya/kv-cache-abort`

priya: PR size: keep < 400 lines changed per PR if possible. For larger work split into a prep PR + followups.

matt: :thumbsup: Also include a checklist in PR description:
- What changed
- Why
- How to test
- Risk
- Rollout plan (if applied)

We have a PR template in .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md

maya: Where's the code style guide? I couldn't find it.

alex: docs: repo root has CONTRIBUTING.md and STYLE.md. Quick links:
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/engine/CONTRIBUTING.md
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/engine/STYLE.md

devex-bot: Pro tip: run `git rebase -i origin/main` before force-pushing. To squash locally:

```
git rebase -i HEAD~3
# change 'pick' to 'squash' for commits to merge
git push --force-with-lease origin your-branch
```
\nmaya: If CI fails after merge, what's the rollback process?

matt: We prefer forward fixes. If it's a release-hotfix we cut a revert PR referencing the commit. For Hosted infra impacting latency we escalate to eng-sre oncall and open an incident.

priya: One more: make sure you update the changelog if the change is user-visible. We auto-generate from Conventional Commits but small docs changes need manual note.

maya: Amazing, thanks everyone! I'll update my branch and re-run pre-commit before pushing. cc @alex if you can eyeball it.

alex: Happy to review — ping me once it's ready. :wave:
